name: Question 14
problem: What is the complex conjugate of $z=-4\text{i}?$
worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate, we flip the sign of the imaginary part.

In the given number $z=-4\text{i},$ the imaginary part is $-4\text{i}$ (there is no real part, just an imaginary part). Flipping the sign, we get $4\text{i}.$

Therefore, the complex conjugate is given by $\overset{―}{z}=4\text{i}.$

Question 14

What is the complex conjugate of z=−4i?

a
z―=4i
b
z―=1−4i
c
z―=4+4i
d
z―=1+4i
e
z―=14i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the complex conjugate, we flip the sign of the imaginary part.

In the given number z=−4i, the imaginary part is −4i (there is no real part, just an imaginary part). Flipping the sign, we get 4i.

Therefore, the complex conjugate is given by z―=4i.
